title: Pool fd double-close protection: fd cleared from slot before it is returned
description:
In crypto2dev_pool_acquire(), when a slot with a ready fd is found:
    pool->slots[i].in_use = 1;
    fd = pool->slots[i].fd;
    pool->slots[i].fd = -1;  // cleared BEFORE returning to caller

The fd is removed from the pool entry before being given to the caller. If wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() runs concurrently (or in a signal handler), it iterates the pool under the lock and skips slots where fd == -1. It does not try to close the borrowed fd.

A future contributor who 'simplifies' this by not clearing pool->slots[i].fd = -1 would introduce a race: cleanup would close an fd that a cipher/hash operation is actively using, converting a crypto operation into reads/writes on an unrelated file.

The pattern is intentional and correct. It matches the same double-close avoidance used in connection pool designs.
